questions.question: Explain the difference between individualist and collectivist cultures and how this affects communication.
questions.correctAnswer: Individualist cultures value independence and direct communication; collectivist cultures value interdependence and indirect communication. In individualist cultures, speaking directly is valued; in collectivist cultures, preserving harmony and avoiding confrontation is prioritised. These differences affect workplace, social and family communication.

questions.question: Describe how culture influences conformity, referring to Smith & Bond's meta-analysis.
questions.correctAnswer: Smith & Bond's meta-analysis found that conformity rates were higher in collectivist cultures (e.g. 37% in Japan vs 25% in the US for Asch-type tasks). This is because conformity serves different functions: in collectivist cultures it maintains group harmony (positive); in individualist cultures it is seen as weakness (negative). The meaning of conformity is culturally constructed.

questions.question: Full-Mark Response Evaluate the importance of considering culture in psychological research, discussing the limitations of WEIRD samples. <div class="
questions.correctAnswer: A grade 9 response will: define WEIRD and explain the problem (unrepresentative samples); describe Henrich et al.'s findings (WEIRD outliers on many measures); explain how culture affects key findings (conformity, self-concept, communication); evaluate the counter-argument (some findings are universal; biological processes are shared); conclude: cultural bias is a significant limitation in psychology, and researchers must test across cultures. However, the solution is not to dismiss Western research but to supplement it with cross-cultural replication. Culture matters but so do universal human processes.
